newsitem.title: USA: CPC says N.American corn refining difficult.
newsitem.headline: CPC says N.American corn refining difficult.

text.p: CPC International said Monday that the North American corn refining market continues to be difficult but said the company reported a strong comeback in its Latin American corn refining operations.

"The corn refining business continues to suffer from the difficult market situation in North America, where current industry overcapacity in the high fructose sector and the resulting competitive pressure are having a highly negative effect on prices and margins," said CPC chairman and chief executive C. R. Shoemate.

"I am gratified, however, by the strong comeback of the Latin American corn refining operations and am confident that the gradual restoration of the supply/demand balance in the North American high fructose business, together with a refocusing of CPC's corn refining business overall, will put the total business on a strong foundation for the future," he added. "Our corn refining plants are among the most cost-efficient in the industry, and the long-time international presence of this business is providing an extensive market area for growth in sales and profits."

CPC International Inc on Monday said it reported a first-quarter gain in earnings per common share for its continuing operations of 9.7 percent to $0.79 per share, compared to $0.72 in the same period last year on a comparable basis.
